newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope appeals for end to fighting in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Pope appeals for end to fighting in Zaire.

text.p: Pope John Paul appealed on Monday for an end to fighting in eastern Zaire, saying conditions there were "an insult to human dignity".

"No man of goodwill can ignore the fate of these people who, in the regions touched by violence, live in conditions which are an insult to human dignity and where life is constantly endangered," he said in a speech to Zairean bishops who met him at the Vatican.
The Pope called for rapid solutions to the problems faced by thousands of Rwandan and displaced Zairean refugees in eastern Zaire living in makeshift conditions.

"I deplore keenly the attacks against people, as well as the looting and destruction suffered by the institutions and the church properties in several of your dioceses which, often, were the only working social structures left," he said.
The Pope hoped that elections that the Zairean government wants to hold in July would be able to go ahead and would allow the country to return to democratic life.
He said the Church was above partisan politics and wanted only to promote democracy.

Civil war has raged in Zaire for four months, with rebels under Laurent Kabila controlling most of the eastern part after launching a war in October to oust president Mobutu Sese Seko, in power since 1965.
Kabila appealed to the United Nations on Sunday to help 170,000 Hutu refugees who fled a camp his troops overran but said there could be no immediate ceasefire.
The United Nations refugee agency UNHCR said on Monday it had lost trace of the 170,000 in the jungle.
An estimated 800,000 Tutsis died in a 1994 genocide in Rwanda blamed on majority Hutus who then fled to eastern Zaire.
